At the ends of the two rubber strips there is a piece of soft sheepskin (length negligible) made into a pouch. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a “Y”-shaped slingshot. On the left are the slingshot fork and handle. The two fixing points of the rubber strips on the slingshot fork are separated up and down, and beside them the span is marked as L; the two rubber strips connect obliquely rightward from these two fixing points to the soft sheepskin pouch on the right, with the projectile placed inside the pouch. The two rubber strips are approximately symmetric about the middle launching direction. Reasoning: Treat the pouch as a point. The distance between the two fixing points is L, so when the pouch is on the perpendicular bisector, each rubber strip and the launching centerline form a right triangle: the hypotenuse is the instantaneous length ell of the rubber strip, the vertical half-spacing is L/2, and the projection along the centerline is sqrt(ell^2-(L/2)^2). Let the angle between the rubber strip and the centerline be theta, then cos theta = sqrt(ell^2-(L/2)^2)/ell. The free length of each rubber strip is L and it satisfies Hooke’s law, so the tension T = k(ell-L). The vertical components of the two rubber strips on the pouch cancel each other, and the components along the launching centerline add, so the magnitude of the force exerted by the pouch on the projectile is F = 2T cos theta = 2k(ell-L) sqrt(ell^2-(L/2)^2)/ell. During the launching process ell gradually decreases from a larger value, and the above expression increases as ell increases, so the maximum force occurs when each rubber strip reaches the maximum length ell=3L. Substituting gives: T = k(3L-L)=2kL, cos theta = sqrt((3L)^2-(L/2)^2)/(3L) = sqrt(35L^2/4)/(3L) = sqrt(35)/6. Therefore F_max = 2·2kL·sqrt(35)/6 = (2/3)sqrt(35) kL.
